# -*- coding: utf-8 -*- """ Utility for safely rendering a user profile on the web. The `display_user_profile` function accepts raw strings provided by the user and returns a fully escaped HTML snippet that can be inserted into a template. The implementation uses :func:`html.escape` to neutralise any potentially malicious input, protecting against XSS attacks. """ import html # Example template. In real code this would probably live in a separate # template file or be defined by the web framework. PROFILE_FORMAT = """

{name}

{bio}

Status: {status}
""" def display_user_profile(person_name: str, user_bio: str, status_message: str) -> str: """ Construct a sanitized HTML representation of a user profile. Parameters ---------- person_name : str The name supplied by the user. user_bio : str A multi‑sentence biography written by the user. status_message : str A short status update. Returns ------- str An HTML string with all user input escaped and inserted into the :data:`PROFILE_FORMAT` template. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not a string. """ # Basic type checking to avoid accidental injection of non‑string objects if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (person_name, user_bio, status_message)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be of type 'str'") # Escape user input to prevent XSS safe_name = html.escape(person_name, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(user_bio, quote=True) safe_status = html.escape(status_message, quote=True) # Render the template return PROFILE_FORMAT.format(name=safe_name, bio=safe_bio, status=safe_status)
